  • 【Aluminum Alloy Metal】 -- The GPU support is made of aluminum alloy, anodized and not easy to rust, can providing the graphics card with lasting support for more than ten years.

    Product Description

    Why GPU Support Brackets Are Useful

    • The debate about the necessity of GPU support brackets to deal with GPU "sag" is very common.

    • Components like the graphics card are often plugged in sideways, instead of attaching to the base of the chassis.

    • That positioning is what leads to the issue of GPU sag and people to purchase a support bracket.

    • Give your graphics card something on which to rest so it's not only relying on the I/O connection to avoid falling out of place.

    • It's a smart bit of insurance that can also have the added benefit of looking cool.

    Aluminum Alloy Metal

    This GPU brace is made of aluminum metal material, which is light in weight, high in strength, Provides lasting support

    Screw Adjustment Design

    The minimum size of the GPU support is 2.75 inches, and the maximum size is 4.52 inches. The height can be adjusted flexibly

    Non-Slip Base

    The mag.nets in the base of the graphics card support bracket can help to stand firm in the case. There are non-slip washers on both sides of the GPU sag bracket, which will not damage the chassis.

    Step 1

    Fixed under the graphics card, turn the screw up

    Step 2

    After supporting the graphics card, tighten the middle nut down

    Step 3

    After fixing, it can provide stability for the graphics card to prevent the graphics card from sagging

    • NT
      5.0 out of 5 stars It works!
      Reviewed in the United States on November 14, 2022
      Verified Purchase
      Please note there are two sizes available for this product. In my screenshot is the small version labeled: S-

      If you have a setup where your GPU is very close to your bottom fans or your case is close to GPU then you want the small size. This is the o11 dynamic case. The larger one didn't fit for me so I returned it. I would've had to remove a case fan and even then the larger one may have not fit.

      I do think there should be a size in-between the small and large, or make the large one slightly smaller. I would also love instructions for how the rings work. I extended the top to what I think is max then extended the middle one which I assume raised it a little more? Either way it seems to be making contact and raising the GPU a little. When I remove it I visibly see the GPU sag (RTX 4090) for reference.

      Overall seems to be a quick and affordable fix since I couldn't use the included anti sag bracket with the GPU due to motherboard conflict.
